# Derivation 3.7A — Scalar nonstationary action candidate {#sec-derivation-03-07A-scalar-nonstationary .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix records the scalar time-dependent equation supported by the
reviewed point-carrier action, including its positive free mode, retarded
solution, stationary recovery, and reciprocal work ledger.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** nonstationary scalar candidate.
- **Regime:** linear weak response about the asymptotic background, with
  collisionless point carriers and action time $t_*$.
- **Status:** action-supported PDE and point-carrier work closure; not an
  interacting physical gravity baseline.
- **Non-claim:** the appendix does not derive bound-matter sourcing,
  $\gamma=1$ operational readout, emission phenomenology, screening, or a
  tensor waveform sector.

## Definitions

$t_*$ is the evolution parameter of the carrier--field action, normalized to
the asymptotic clock. The content-density notation is

$$
\rho_M:=\frac{\mathcal M}{c},
$$

so $[\rho_M]=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ in the cold static calibration.

The scalar field and carriers are governed by

$$
S_\theta=\frac Z2\int dt_*d^3x
\left(\frac{\dot\theta^2}{c^2}-|\nabla\theta|^2\right),
$$

$$
H_a=N(\theta)c
\sqrt{p_{f,a}^2+Q(\theta)p_a^2}.
\tag{3.7A.1}
$$

At the weak point,

$$
N=1-\alpha\theta+\cdots,
\qquad
Q=1-2\alpha\gamma\theta+\cdots,
$$

and Newtonian normalization fixes

$$
Z=\frac{\alpha^2c^4}{4\pi G_N}>0.
\tag{3.7A.2}
$$

## Linear equation and source status

Variation gives

$$
\Box\theta
=\frac{4\pi G_N}{\alpha c^3}
\left(\mathcal M+\gamma\mathcal C_{kk}\right),
\qquad
\Box:=\frac1{c^2}\partial_{t_*}^2-\Delta.
\tag{3.7A.3}
$$

The current content-only stationary source package corresponds, within this
single-shell scalar completion, to $\gamma=0$. With the normalized choice
$\alpha=1$,

$$
\boxed{
\Box\theta=\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^2}\rho_M}.
\tag{3.7A.4}
$$

This branch preserves the stationary Poisson map and exact local $c$ with its
carrier-derived clock and ruler. It does not provide the standard
$\gamma=1$ weak-light response. The $\gamma=1$ alternative changes the
point-carrier source to $\mathcal M+\mathcal C_{kk}$ and is not adopted or
interaction-closed.

## Retarded solution and stationary recovery

For compact prescribed weak source data, Equation (3.7A.4) has the retarded
solution

$$
\boxed{
\theta(t_*,\mathbf x)
=\frac{G_N}{c^2}\int
\frac{\rho_M(t_*-R/c,\mathbf x')}{R}\,d^3x'},
\qquad
R:=|\mathbf x-\mathbf x'|.
\tag{3.7A.5}
$$

When time derivatives vanish,

$$
\Delta\theta=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^2}\rho_M,
$$

$$
\theta(\mathbf x)
=\frac{G_N}{c^2}\int
\frac{\rho_M(\mathbf x')}{R}\,d^3x',
\tag{3.7A.6}
$$

which is exactly the weak stationary scalar map. The source history in
Equation (3.7A.5) must come from a conserved matter model; an arbitrary
prescribed function is only an external-source approximation.

## Positive mode and reciprocal work

The conjugate momentum and field Hamiltonian are

$$
\pi_\theta=\frac Z{c^2}\dot\theta,
$$

$$
H_\theta=\int d^3x
\left(\frac{c^2\pi_\theta^2}{2Z}
+\frac Z2|\nabla\theta|^2\right).
\tag{3.7A.7}
$$

Because $Z>0$, the free scalar has one positive mode per nonzero wave vector,

$$
\omega^2=c^2k^2.
$$

Let

$$
\Xi(\mathbf x)
:=\sum_a\frac{\partial H_a}{\partial\theta}
\delta^{(3)}(\mathbf x-\mathbf x_a).
$$

The field energy satisfies

$$
\partial_{t_*}u_\theta+\nabla\cdot\mathbf S_\theta
=-\Xi\dot\theta,
$$

and the carrier energy satisfies the opposite equation after its transport
flux is included. Thus the displayed point-carrier action has reciprocal local
and integrated work. This does not establish positivity or localization for
arbitrary binding and interaction energies.

## Operational content

The same action supplies clocks, rulers, and trajectories:

$$
d\tau=N\,dt_*,
\qquad
d\ell^2=Q^{-1}\delta_{ij}dx^i dx^j,
\qquad
\frac{d\ell}{d\tau}=c\quad\text{for }p_f=0.
$$

These observables make the scalar mode more than a free formal PDE. Its status
nevertheless remains a point-carrier candidate because the interacting source
and the physical $\gamma=1$ readout are not jointly closed.

## Result

The scalar equation has a positive action-supported free mode, causal retarded
propagation at $c$, exact stationary recovery, and reciprocal point-carrier
work. It is a disciplined nonstationary candidate, not a promoted physical
gravity baseline.
